Calculate Spatial Distance Decay Weights

Source: R/01-decay_functions.R
calc_decay.Rd

Calculate weights using different spatial decay functions or a custom function. Supports built-in methods and custom decay functions. The decay weights represent how the influence or interaction strength diminishes with distance.

Usage

calc_decay(distance, method = "gaussian", sigma = NULL, snap = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

distance

Numeric vector, matrix, or SpatRaster of distances

method

Character string specifying the decay function or a custom function: "gaussian", "exponential", "power", "inverse", "binary", or function(distance, ...); or a kernel declared with decay_kernel

sigma

Parameter controlling the rate of decay. A single number, or a SpatRaster aligned to distance (1 layer, or one per layer) for a spatially varying catchment (variable-catchment FCA / V2SFCA). A declared custom kernel needs a single positive number within its bounds.

snap

Logical; if TRUE, skip input validation

...

Additional parameters for custom decay functions, or the offset c of the "inverse" kernel. A declared custom kernel takes none: its fixed arguments belong to the declaration.

Value

Object of the same class as input containing decay weights

Details

Built-in kernels for a distance \(d\), and the sigma used when none is given:

  • "gaussian": \(\exp(-d^2 / (2\sigma^2))\); default \(\sigma = 11.64884\).

  • "exponential": \(\exp(-\sigma d)\); default \(\sigma = 0.1\).

  • "power": \(d^{-\sigma}\); default \(\sigma = 2\). The weight is Inf at distance 0, which the FCA functions refuse.

  • "inverse": \(1 / (d + c)\), with c = 1 unless c is passed in ...; sigma does not enter the weights (a given value is still validated).

  • "binary": 1 when \(d \le \sigma\), otherwise 0; default \(\sigma = 97.5\).

The defaults are historical values, not recommendations: set sigma for the units and scale of your travel times.

A kernel declared with decay_kernel can be given as method. A built-in declaration behaves exactly like its name. A declared custom kernel needs sigma, a single positive number within the bounds of the declaration, and takes its fixed arguments from the declaration, so ... must be empty; a SpatRaster sigma is refused. It is evaluated on the finite distances only: a missing distance has the weight NA and an infinite distance (an absent edge) the weight 0, as with the built-in kernels. A negative or non-finite weight at a finite distance is an error. A vector or matrix keeps its shape, and a SpatRaster keeps its geometry, layer names and missing cells; it is read into memory for a declared kernel.

Examples

library(terra)

# Distances on a small 10 x 10 grid
r <- rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = 0, ymax = 10)
values(r) <- 1:100

# Built-in decay functions
w <- c(
  calc_decay(r, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30),
  calc_decay(r, method = "exponential", sigma = 0.1),
  calc_decay(r, method = "power", sigma = 2),
  calc_decay(r, method = "binary", sigma = 50)
)
names(w) <- c("gaussian", "exponential", "power", "binary")
plot(w)


# A custom decay function receives the distances and its own arguments
gaussian_power <- function(distance, sigma = 30, power = 2, ...) {
  exp(-(distance^2) / (2 * sigma^2)) * distance^(-power)
}
w_custom <- calc_decay(r, method = gaussian_power, sigma = 30, power = 1.5)

# A declared kernel records its meaning, bounds and fixed arguments
plateau <- decay_kernel(
  function(distance, sigma, plateau = 5) {
    ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)))
  },
  name = "plateau", parameter = "scale", args = list(plateau = 5)
)
w_plateau <- calc_decay(r, method = plateau, sigma = 10)

# One layer per facility gives one layer of weights per facility
distances <- rast(replicate(3, r))
names(distances) <- c("facility1", "facility2", "facility3")
weights <- calc_decay(distances, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30)
